questions.question: Explain free-space wireless communication and list the limitations associated with it. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• (Explanation 3 Marks, limitations 2 marks)
  • Free-space wireless communication refers to the transmission of electromagnetic waves
  • through air or vacuum without any guiding medium such as cables or fibers. The signal
  • propagates directly from transmitter to receiver through line-of-sight or indirect paths.
  • Limitations:
  • • High path loss due to signal spreading
  • • Susceptibility to atmospheric conditions (rain, fog, etc.)
  • • Interference from other wireless signals
  • • Limited range without repeaters
  • • Multipath fading in urban environments

questions.question: Describe the Bluetooth protocol stack. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• (5 layers – 1 mark each)
  • The Bluetooth proto col stack is a layered architecture used for short -range wireless
  • communication.
  • It consists of:
  • • Radio Layer: Handles physical transmission of signals.
  • • Baseband Layer: Manages link establishment and packet handling.
  • • Link Manager Protocol (LMP): Controls authentication, encryption, and power modes.
  • • L2CAP (Logical Link Control and Adaptation Protocol): Provides multiplexing and
  • segmentation.
  • • Upper Layers: Includes RFCOMM (serial communication), SDP (service discovery),
  • and application profiles.
  • Bluetooth enables low-power, short-range communication between devices such as phones,
  • laptops, and IoT devices.

questions.question: Explain the concept of blocks and flowgraphs in GNU Radio. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• (blocks – 2.5 marks, flowgraph – 2.5 marks)
  • In GNU Radio, signal processing is designed using graphical models.
  • • Blocks: These are basic processing units such as filters, modulators, demodulators, or
  • signal sources/sinks.
  • • Flowgraphs: A flowgraph is a graphical representation of signal flow created by
  • connecting blocks.
  • Each block performs a specific function, and data flows from source blocks to sink blocks
  • through processing blocks. Flowgraphs can be built using GNU Radio Companion (GRC),
  • making SDR design flexible and modular.

questions.question: Explain the basic principle of operation of GPS. / [CO2] [5x4 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• (Explanation – 5 marks)
  • The Global Positioning System (GPS) works based on satellite triangulation.
  • • A GPS receiver gets signals from at least four satellites.
  • • Each satellite sends its position and time information.
  • • The receiver calculates the distance using signal travel time.
  • • Using trilateration, the exact position (latitude, longitude, altitude) is determined.
  • GPS works globally and is widely used in navigation, mapping, and tracking applications.

questions.question: Explain the basic principle of modulation and justify the need for modulation in wireless communication with respect to antenna height, interference, and multiplexing. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• ( Basic principle, AM, FM, PM – 5 marks, need for modulation – 5 marks)
  • Modulation is the process of varying a high-frequency carrier signal in accordance with a low-
  • frequency information (message) signal. It enables efficient transmission of signals over long
  • distances in wireless communication.
  • A message signal (baseband) is superimposed on a carrier wave by varying its:
  • • Amplitude → AM (Amplitude Modulation)
  • • Frequency → FM (Frequency Modulation)
  • • Phase → PM (Phase Modulation)

questions.question: With neat block diagrams, explain AM and FM transmitters and highlight the key differences between them. / [CO1] [10x2 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• (AM transmitter – block diagram -2marks, explanation -2marks, FM transmitter –
  • block diagram – 2 marks, explanation – 2 marks, difference – 1 marks)
  • AM transmitter
  • An Amplitude Modulation (AM) transmitter is a device that encodes audio or data onto a
  • high-frequency carrier wave by varying the wave's amplitude. It operates in the medium
  • frequency (MF) band (535 to 1705 kHz) and is used in broadcasting, aviation, and DIY
  • radio testing.
  • Working
  • • Message signal is combined with carrier
  • • Amplitude of carrier varies
  • • Signal transmitted via antenna
  • FM transmitter
  • An FM (Frequency Modulation) transmitter takes an audio signal (like a voice or music)
  • and encodes it onto a high -frequency radio wave for wireless transmissio n. The
  • transmission process sequentially processes the audio signal, generates a carrier wave,
  • combines them, and prepares the final signal for broadcast.
